outcome: neonate admission into intensive care unit
cohort: The study included 62 women, with 26 having congenital uterine malformations and 36 serving as controls, who delivered in one university-affiliated medical center between 2010 and 2017.
finding: Uterine congenital malformations are an independent risk factor for pregnancy complications, with significantly higher rates of preterm delivery, lower Apgar scores, and increased neonate admission to the intensive care unit.
mod_finding: The cesarean section rate was 64.3% in the group of women with uterine malformations.
